bib.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "AUTOMEM: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill", Shengguang Wu, Hao Zhu, Yuhui Zhang, Xiaohan Wang, Serena Yeung-Levy (Stanford). Preprint, arXiv:2607.01224v1 [cs.AI], 1 Jul 2026. Code: github.com/autoLearnMem/AutoMem.
COVERAGE: Read all 60,339 chars, main text, limitations, appendices A and B. The reference list was skimmed past the "Memory-R1" entry. Table 1 and the figure data were read as extracted.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Scaffold optimisation alone (no weight change) lifts a file-system-memory agent 1.9x to 3.7x over its own v0 file-memory scaffold.
   number: Crafter 25.0->47.27, MiniHack 7.5->27.5, NetHack 0.42->1.57 (progression %).
   setup: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, BALROG games, 10 seeds (42-51), mean±SE; Crafter n=10, MiniHack 5 per task x 8 tasks, NetHack n=5. The meta-LLM is Claude Opus 4.6.
   quote: "Crafter 25.0% →47.27% (×1.89), MiniHack 7.5%→27.5% (×3.67), NetHack 0.42%→1.57% (×3.74) (Table 1, Figure 1)."
   where: Sec 3.2, p.6-7.
2. Memory-proficiency training adds a smaller gain on top of the scaffold. A LoRA "memory specialist" is trained while the gameplay model stays frozen.
   number: 51.36 / 30.0 / 1.85.
   setup: Trained on the agent's own traces, selected by Claude Opus 4.7. Training sets: 1597 examples (Crafter), 444 (MiniHack), 800 (NetHack). The gains are within one SE on MiniHack and NetHack (e.g. 30.00±7.25 vs 27.50±7.06).
   quote: "the memory- proficiency training loop lifts progression to 51.36% on Crafter (+4.09), 30.0% on MiniHack (+2.5), and 1.85% on NetHack (+0.28)"
   where: Sec 3.2, p.6-7.
3. Memory-managed 32B matches frontier models and beats a larger model.
   number: Opus-4.5 49.5/27.5/2.0; Qwen2.5-72B 27.3/5.0/0.3.
   setup: Frontier and 72B numbers are taken from the BALROG leaderboard, not rerun. The 32B memory agent was tuned per game on the same eval seeds.
   quote: "comparable to Claude-Opus-4.5 (Crafter/MiniHack/NetHack: 49.5/27.5/2.0) and within a few points of Gemini-3.1-Pro-Thinking (55.0/27.5/2.6)."
   where: Sec 3.2.
4. Plain context management is far weaker than structured file memory.
   number: sliding window 19.55 / 2.50 / 0.00; with chain-of-thought 17.27 / 10.00 / 0.00.
   setup: same Qwen2.5-32B and BALROG harness, sliding window of the 16 most recent observations.
   quote: "sliding window 19.55±3.46 2.50±2.47 0.00±0.00 + chain-of-thought 17.27±2.71 10.00±4.74 0.00±0.00"
   where: Table 1, p.6.
5. Naive file memory (v0) barely beats a sliding window, and on Crafter the v0 score is below the sliding-window score only by noise. Structure matters more than having a store.
   number: v0 = 25.00 / 7.50 / 0.42, versus window 19.55 / 2.50 / 0.00.
   quote: "memory-as-file-system,v025.00±5.50 7.50±4.16 0.42±0.37"
   where: Table 1. This is my reading of the table, not an author claim. The SEs overlap.
6. Verbatim-append stores bloat and hurt. The fix is coordinate-keyed upsert (overwrite, don't append) plus auto-synced state files, which cut memory growth and input tokens.
   number: per-step growth 138 -> 6 chars (-95%); redundant writes -68 to -83%; input tokens/step -3 to -30%; unproductive action rate -32 to -65%.
   setup: NetHack for the 95% figure; v0 vs final scaffold.
   quote: "its per-step growth falls from 138 to 6 characters, a 95% reduction."
   where: Sec 3.2, Fig 4 and 5.
7. Training teaches consult-before-write. Memory writes per SEARCH fall in the LOG phase.
   number: Crafter 0.84->0.39, MiniHack 2.89->0.82, NetHack 4.66->1.31.
   quote: "Crafter 0.84→0.39 (−54%), MiniHack 2.89→0.82 (−72%), and NetHack 4.66→1.31 (−72%)."
   where: Table 2, p.8.

BASELINES
- No-memory: none. There is no run with the model given nothing.
- Full-context: none run. The nearest is the BALROG sliding window of 16 recent observations, with and without CoT.
- Simple RAG or vector store: none. Retrieval is model-issued SEARCH over text files.
- Distilled versus raw memory: no ablation. The v0 file-memory agent stands in as "raw" and the evolved scaffold as structured. Gains bundle many changes, so they are not isolated (see Appendix B).
- Skill library: none. Voyager is mentioned only in related work. The "skill" in the title means a trainable metamemory skill, not a library of procedures.
- Appendix B shows that much of the scaffold gain is hand-style game logic written by the meta-LLM (craft preconditions, "descend now" directives, pre-loaded game knowledge, action blocking). It is not purely memory.

LIMITS
- Authors concede: the memory is episodic only (the file system resets each episode); the tasks are games only; a separate scaffold and specialist were optimised per game, so cross-environment sharing is untested.
- Not shown: there is no ablation separating memory content from scaffold hints and guardrails. The eval seeds (42-51) are reused as the gate for accepting scaffold revisions. Training seeds are disjoint, but scaffold selection is tuned on the eval seeds, so the scaffold numbers are optimistic.
- Small n (5 NetHack episodes); NetHack absolute scores are tiny (under 2%).
- Frontier numbers come from the leaderboard and may use different harness settings from the Qwen runs.
- The meta-LLMs are expensive frontier models (Opus 4.6 and 4.7). No cost accounting is given.
- The claim that memory beats scale is based on one comparison (Qwen 32B versus 72B) using a different harness.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
Metamemory: Flavell 1979; Nelson 1990. Extended mind: Clark & Chalmers 1998. RAG: Lewis et al. 2020 (NeurIPS). MemGPT: Packer et al. 2023 (arXiv). Generative Agents: Park et al. 2023 (UIST). A-MEM: Xu et al. 2025. MemoryBank: Zhong et al. 2024. MemLLM: Modarressi et al. 2024. Self-Notes: Lanchantin et al. 2023 (NeurIPS). MemAct: Zhang et al. 2025b. MemSkill: Zhang et al. 2026a. MeMo: Quek et al. 2026. MemEvolve: Zhang et al. 2025a. EvolveMem: Liu et al. 2026. CoALA: Sumers et al. 2023 (TMLR). Voyager: Wang et al. 2023a. Reflexion: Shinn et al. 2023 (NeurIPS). ExpeL: Zhao et al. 2024. ReAct: Yao et al. 2022. ADAS: Hu et al. 2024. DSPy: Khattab et al. 2023. LoRA: Hu et al. 2022 (ICLR). BALROG: Paglieri et al. 2024. Crafter: Hafner 2021. MiniHack: Samvelyan et al. 2021. NLE: Küttler et al. 2020 (NeurIPS).

CODE: none worth keeping. The memory action tokens are <|APPEND|>, <|SEARCH|> and <|UPSERT_MAP|> (Sec 1 and Fig 5).

FIGURES (one candidate)
- Fig 5, p.8, "Example memory file evolution (NetHack)". It shows the append-only dungeon_map with duplicate coordinates becoming a coordinate-keyed UPSERT map with auto-synced inventory and status files. This is a concrete picture of raw append versus a maintained, distilled store. Alternative: Fig 4, p.7, four bar panels of v0 versus optimised behaviour. Fig 1 and Fig 3 are the headline gain curves and the architecture.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The extraction is clean, but figure text is interleaved with the body text. Figure 1 values were not extracted, so I have only the Table 1 numbers.
